findings.issue: Home page inlines its own `<ul class="card-grid">` with PokemonCard instead of reusing CardList, because CardList can't forward the `types` prop
findings.suggestion: Add an optional per-card types mapping to CardList (or accept a typed card DTO) and delete the inline copy, so card lists exist once

findings.issue: Client component hardcodes the API media sprite scheme (`${apiBase}/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png`), duplicating data-source knowledge that the server layer otherwise owns
findings.suggestion: Include the sprite URL in the Card/IndexEntry DTOs produced server-side (as already done for artwork in app/server/api/pokemon/[name].get.ts:33) so the component just renders it

findings.issue: The NotFound/error-state/data template triple is duplicated across pokemon, moves, abilities and types pages
findings.suggestion: Extract a small wrapper or composable handling 404→NotFound, other-error message, and the data branch

findings.issue: Ability-specific `hidden` flag is threaded through the generic Card type, CardList, PokemonCard and speciesCards
findings.suggestion: Keep the card DTO generic; pass the 'Hidden ability' note as slot/prop at the one call site that needs it

findings.issue: Client re-implements the typeRef label fallback (`typeLabels.get(t) ?? humanize(t)`), duplicating app/server/utils/data.ts:66
findings.suggestion: Have /api/species return TypeRef objects (or move the fallback into #shared) so the mapping exists once

findings.issue: error.vue duplicates app.vue's header/nav/footer markup (incl. the legal footer text in two files)
findings.suggestion: Extract a layout component (AppHeader/AppFooter) used by both app.vue and error.vue

findings.issue: typeLabels()/allTypes() re-fetch and re-map all type details on every request that calls them (species, pokemon, moves endpoints)
findings.suggestion: Cache the derived label map (or the TypeInfo list) alongside the raw-response cache in pokeapi.ts

summary: This is a well-seamed Nuxt 4 app: an anti-corruption /api layer with a shared DTO contract, one PokeAPI client owning fetching/caching, and small prop-driven components, so most fixes and removals land in one obvious place. The main editability gaps are the home page bypassing CardList (duplicated card-grid markup), the sprite URL scheme leaking into PokemonCard, and small render conventions (404 handling, type-label fallback) duplicated across pages. Extending to a new section is mostly reuse with only a thin pattern copy.
